title: Programming Foundations
content: Software engineering is the disciplined creation of reliable, maintainable software. Programming is instructing a computer via code. KEY CONCEPTS: Variables, data types, control flow (if/loops), functions, data structures (arrays, objects). Syntax vs logic. WORKED EXAMPLE: A function that takes inputs, processes them, returns output — the building block of all software. PRACTICE: 1) Write pseudocode for a login check. 2) List 4 data types. 3) Explain a loop's purpose.

title: Data Structures & Algorithms
content: Data structures organize data; algorithms process it efficiently. KEY CONCEPTS: Arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash maps, trees, graphs. Big-O notation (time/space complexity). Sorting and searching. WORKED EXAMPLE: A hash map gives O(1) lookup vs O(n) for scanning an array. title: Software Design & Architecture
content: Good architecture makes software maintainable and scalable. WORKED EXAMPLE: MVC separates data (model), display (view), and logic (controller) so each changes independently.
